items.stem: A chat app sends a new message by calling the same endpoint again whenever the connection drops before a reply arrives. The server stores one message per request it receives. Which method choice makes these automatic retries safest?

options.text: POST /messages, since the server assigns IDs
PUT /messages/{id}, with an ID the client generates
PATCH /messages, since it only adds one item
GET /messages/new, since it needs no request body

items.stem: A client sends POST /accounts with an email address that is already registered. The JSON is valid and the fields pass validation. Which status code best describes this outcome?

options.text: 200 OK, with an error message in the body
409 Conflict, since it clashes with current state
500 Internal Server Error, since the save failed
404 Not Found, since the account does not exist

items.stem: A client calls DELETE /notes/9 twice in a row. The first call removes the note and the second finds nothing. In one sentence, why is DELETE still called idempotent even though the two responses can differ?
Each call to POST /tickets creates one new ticket. A client sends the same POST /tickets request 3 times and every request succeeds. How many tickets exist afterwards, starting from none?

A client sends PUT /profiles/4 with only {"bio": "Hello"} to a server that follows PUT's replace semantics. Which method should the client have used to change only the bio, and what is at risk with the PUT?
